title: Yellow, and just the seen
hookLine: lemon, butter, school bus: every yellow comes with a story. the yellow disc asks for just the color.
carry: in the seen, just the seen
tomorrow: what do you see first: red, or the story about red?

cards: Paint stores give their yellows names: lemon, butter, school bus, sunflower. Every name drags something in with it, a smell, a memory, a ride to school. Buddhaghosa's yellow disc asks for the opposite.
A bed of golden flowers, or yellow cloth, set in front of you, and only the plain word: yellow, yellow. No lemon. No school bus.
Not even flower. Which is yesterday's question: what happens if you just look at yellow, and nothing else? At first, honestly, the mind gets restless and starts adding.

teach.h: SET DOWN THE NAME AND THE STORY.
teach.b: Start with what the instruction takes away. A yellow flower is a thing with a name, a stalk, a smell and a story: grandma grew these. The disc asks you to set all that down and take the color as the color.
It's harder than it sounds, because the mind loves to add. The suttas have a short teaching that names the same move.
A seeker called Bahiya stops the Buddha on his alms round and won't wait: teach me now. The Buddha gives him a few lines.

teach.h: IN THE SEEN, JUST THE SEEN.
teach.b: In the seen, let there be just the seen. In the heard, just the heard. In the sensed, just the sensed.
When that's so, he says, you aren't caught up in it, and that is the end of suffering.

teach.h: WHERE THE COLOR ENDS, THE STORY STARTS.
teach.b: The text says Bahiya understood right there, in the street. His teaching is insight, not a disc practice, but the two share a gesture: dropping the extra layer. And here's the part worth repeating tonight.
Often what stings in a day isn't the seen at all; it's the layer on top. A face in the hallway is a face. She's ignoring me is the layer.
Looking at plain yellow is practice in noticing where the color ends and the story begins.

how: In Theravada meditation the yellow kasina uses yellow flowers, cloth or other yellow material, noted simply as 'yellow, yellow', as the Visuddhimagga describes; Bahiya's teaching from the Udana is often recited and studied on its own.

o: the golden glow said to surround a holy person
a color for wisdom, worn at festivals and rites
the plain color seen alone, before any name or story

games.q: the seen and the story — tap the pairs.
p: asked on the alms round, wouldn't wait

s: the yellow disc is about thinking of sunshine and joy
the instruction is the plain color and the plain word, yellow. no associations.
Bahiya asked for teaching while the Buddha was on his alms round
the Buddha gave him a few short lines: in the seen, just the seen.
'just the seen' means having no feelings at all
it means noticing the extra layer the mind adds, so you aren't caught up in it.

games.q: a friend walks past you in the hallway without saying hi. by today's teaching, what's just the seen?
o: she's annoyed with you and wants you to know it.
a friend walked by and didn't say hi.
nothing at all happened, so feel nothing about it.
games.why: that's the seen. 'she's annoyed with me' is the layer on top. the teaching doesn't ban feelings; it notices where the seeing ends and the story begins.

practice: Pick up something yellow if one is close, a lemon, a pencil, a sticky note; if not, find yellow anywhere in view. Feel its weight and its temperature first.
Then set the names aside and let your eyes rest on just the color, and when a memory or a judgment shows up, notice it as extra and come back to yellow.

wordCard.voice: Yellow: pita in Pali. The color on its own, before any name or story gets added.

orig.note: Pali: yellow. The color disc held in mind with the plain word, yellow, yellow.

carryVoice: Keep this one: in the seen, just the seen. Yellow, before the story about it arrives. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Visuddhimagga 5 (the yellow kasina: yellow flowers, cloth or other material, as with the blue; noted as 'yellow, yellow')

Udana 1.10 (Bahiya Sutta: Bahiya asks the Buddha on his alms round; 'in the seen will be merely the seen, in the heard merely the heard, in the sensed merely the sensed …'; Bahiya understands on the spot)
